title: The ox-herding pictures
hookLine: Kakuan sets the Zen path out as ten pictures of a herder and his ox, and the last one walks back into town
tomorrow: what has the herder lost, and why doesn't he know it?
last: ONE BREATH · LISTEN FIRST · NAME THE HOME

lines: A HERDER HAS LOST HIS OX.
cards: A storyboard, a comic strip, the little drawings on a flat-pack instruction sheet: some things are easiest to follow in pictures.

A Chinese Zen teacher named Kuoan, known in Japan as Kakuan, set out the whole spiritual path as ten pictures, each with a short poem. In the first, a herder stands in wild, tall grass, searching. He has lost his ox.
Why an ox? Zen teachers read the ox as your own true nature: the very thing you're looking for when you start looking.

teach.b: Then the pictures move. He finds the tracks. He glimpses the ox.
He catches it, and it fights him. He tames it.
He rides it home, playing a flute. Then the ox is forgotten, and the herder sits alone.
Then an empty circle: ox and herder both forgotten. Then the source: a river, a tree, simply as they are. And the tenth picture is the surprise.

The herder walks back into the marketplace, among ordinary people, with open, helping hands. That is the Zen teaching the series carries: the search doesn't end alone on a mountain. It ends back in town, helping.
Look at the week you just walked and you can see the tenth picture in it. A child's first breath. A friend heard out.
A teaching handed on with its home.
Starting tomorrow, the summit walks the ten pictures one at a time, beginning in the tall grass.

how: Zen teachers use the ten ox-herding pictures, with their short poems, to map practice from searching to returning to the marketplace; students look at them and ask which picture they're in.

s: the ox-herding pictures end with the herder alone on a mountain
the popular guess. the tenth picture brings him back into the marketplace, with helping hands.

games.q: your cousin comes home from a long silent retreat and says ordinary life now feels 'less spiritual'. what fits the ox-herding pictures?
o: the last picture is the marketplace: the path ends back among people, helping.
the empty circle is the top; daily life is a step back down from it.
the retreat was the real thing; town is where you wait for the next one.
games.why: the series doesn't stop at the empty circle. picture ten brings the herder back to town, with helping hands.

practice: Let the ten pictures pass through your mind like a slow slideshow: searching, tracks, a glimpse, the catch, the taming, riding home, the ox forgotten, the empty circle, the source, the marketplace.
Notice which one feels most like where you are right now. Then rest in that picture until the bell.
